name: Funastrum

project_scope.selection_mode: Approved Master Plant Pool native/personal iNaturalist pool
project_scope.excluded_duplicate_name: Funastrum cynanchodies from row 489 = misspelling of F. cynanchoides
project_scope.excluded_third_species: Funastrum heterophyllum — legitimate accepted species, externally compared; not in approved local pool pair
project_scope.native_status: range UNRESOLVED pending independent county audit, despite State of Texas Kew nativity

look_here_first: Look at a MATURE LEAF and then ONE SINGLE BLOOM. WAVY/CRISPED narrow triangular leaves plus LARGER (~2 cm) orange-brown/green 5-lobed flowers = F. crispum. Mostly FLAT-edged cordate/ovate leaves plus smaller creamy/rose fringed petals and shiny white plump CORONA = F. cynanchoides. Opposite leaves and twining habit establish milkvine context but do not separate them. Compare axillary flower clusters and five corona lobes; common names overlap.
shared_genus_traits: Twining perennial milky-latex vines in Apocynaceae (former milkweed family Asclepiadaceae), with OPPOSITE simple often heart-based leaves and no true tendrils.
Small to medium five-lobed star corollas in axillary umbel-like cymes, surrounded by five fleshy corona structures that are NOT petals or unopened buds.
Gynostegium is the fused reproductive column of milkweed-family flowers; paired pollinia often inside lateral slots. Teach corolla vs corona vs gynostegium explicitly.
Fruits are follicles splitting along one seam, with brown seeds bearing silky parachutelike coma hairs.
Not all western specimens labeled Sarcostemma cynanchoides are the accepted eastern F. cynanchoides; subsp. hartwegii often F. heterophyllum in FNA.

quick_key.if: Leaf margins distinctly crinkled or wavy on mature leaves, flowers larger with orange/brown/green spreading lobes, corona lobes pinched in middle
Leaf margins generally smooth/flat, petals cream/white flushed rose or pink, smaller flower with swollen gleaming WHITE oval corona lobes
Leaf extremely narrow and linear, purple/pink desert flower, western trans-Pecos or Sonoran source
quick_key.then: Check Funastrum heterophyllum (separate accepted species), not automatically F. cynanchoides

quick_key.if: Many TINY greenish flowers in long branched/raceme-like axillary sprays and smooth plump pods
Large broad reticulate green flower with metallic pearllike center
quick_key.then: Matelea reticulata — pearl milkvine, different genus

species_comparison_matrix.crispum: Frequently waved/crisped (may be nearly flat); narrow-triangular, cordate base
species_comparison_matrix.cynanchoides: Generally plane/flat; ovate to lanceolate, cordate to sometimes hastate base
species_comparison_matrix.weight: strongest on mature same-scale leaves but variable

species_comparison_matrix.crispum: ~20mm across; orange aging brown and green; petals each ~10mm
species_comparison_matrix.cynanchoides: Smaller cream to rosy/lilac; petals ~3–6mm, often rose-tipped

species_comparison_matrix.crispum: Usually glabrous; margined by short ciliate hairs
species_comparison_matrix.cynanchoides: Very finely rough/hispidulous to nearly glabrous, ciliate petal margin

species_comparison_matrix.crispum: Pink/white, constricted or waisted in middle (FNA)
species_comparison_matrix.cynanchoides: Glossy bright white ovoid tips, inflated, not constricted

species_comparison_matrix.crispum: Typically to ~9 flowers on one short peduncle (Williamson flora)
species_comparison_matrix.cynanchoides: Compact rounded/umbel-like cluster of numerous smaller stars

species_comparison_matrix.weight: fruit macros need to be verified

species_comparison_matrix.crispum: Dry rocky slopes, shrubland, Central Texas limestone/canyon habitat
species_comparison_matrix.cynanchoides: Wide disturbed grasslands, mesquite/oak scrub, riparian and limestone areas

comparison_cards.title: Wavyleaf versus climbing milkweed — match a leaf and a flower
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Find a FULL mature leaf at same scale: crispum often waved/crinkled along margin, cynanchoides mostly flat-edged. Now compare an OPEN flower: crispum ~20mm brown/orange/green star vs cynanchoides smaller cream to rosy star. In the center, a clear corona close-up can resolve constricted versus plump unpinched lobes.

field_matrix.cynanchoides: five swollen smooth SHINY WHITE ovoid lobes, not pinched

comparison_cards.caution: Leaf margins and color can vary. Require two or three traits, ideally open flower + intact mature leaf. No substitute photos of western F. heterophyllum.

comparison_cards.title: Twinevine or talayote?
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Follow a leaf to its FLOWER STALK. Funastrum produces a short rounded UMBEL-like bunch of five-pointed pale/brown flowers with conspicuous central white/pink corona. Talayote Cynanchum unifarium makes many tiny green-and-white flowers on a more branched, RACEMELIKE axillary cyme.

field_matrix.funastrum: umbel-like bunch of spreading five-pointed stars
notably five conspicuous petals with distinctive fleshy corona
field_matrix.talayote: tiny (~5mm) green/yellow petals with white edge and central 3-lobed corona lobes
opposite/cordate with white latex — NOT a separator

comparison_cards.caution: Both twine and contain milky latex; avoid identifying from the leaves alone.

comparison_cards.title: Twinevine or pearl milkvine?
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Flower FACE first: pearl milkvine has a LARGE, flat, DARK-NETTED green corolla with distinctive SILVERY pearl. The local Funastrum pair has orange-brown to cream/rose petals and stout pink/white corona lobes, not a dark green netted broad star.

field_matrix.funastrum: small-to-medium brown/orange or cream/rose 5-lobed, often ciliate fringes
field_matrix.matelea: reticulata large dark-netted flat green; edwardsensis pale longitudinal striped bell
reticulata highly reflective silvery anther appendages; edwardsensis raised lobed corona

field_matrix.funastrum: usually thinner, narrower opposite heart-based blades

comparison_cards.caution: Exact comparisons require flower and pod photos; with sterile vines identify to milkvine group if uncertain.

visual_comparison.title: Funastrum: wavy leaf, flower size and five corona lobes
visual_comparison.subtitle: Photographs are exact accepted species and public-domain/CC0. Sources of the western F. heterophyllum complex are excluded. Use the PHOTO and field characters together; image arrows need precise original-photo inspection.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: WAVY leaf + big brown/orange bloom = CRISPUM. FLAT leaf + smaller pale-pink five-star bloom + WHITE oval corona = CYNANCHOIDES. Many tiny green-white flowers in branched spike = TALAYOTE.
